scope: Selected original reported metrics; no rerun or pooling across studies.

questions.question: Can the components be implemented with distinct, inspectable interfaces?
questions.consolidated_answer: Yes, bounded: SH01 shared records; SH02 isolated graph/plan/backend; SC01–CAP01 explicit execution lifecycle.

questions.question: Does supplied hierarchy help learning a maintenance rule?
questions.consolidated_answer: Yes under SH01's fixed recipe and three completed pairs; not a universal dense-attention limitation.

questions.question: Does fewer attention work mean lower latency or memory?
questions.consolidated_answer: Not automatically. SH01 lost on time; SH02 packing helped at larger shapes; total-memory/energy superiority remains unestablished.

questions.question: Can cleanup preserve the original computation?
questions.consolidated_answer: SH02 preserved class decisions and numerical tolerance; historical bitwise replay mismatch remains recorded.

questions.question: Can a bounded workspace handle revisions and interrupted jobs?
questions.consolidated_answer: Yes on SC01/SC02 typed fixtures, with exact source/model binding and explicit deferrals.

questions.question: Does segmentation beat competent conventional caching?
questions.consolidated_answer: Sometimes in time, not universally; no unique answer-quality advantage shown.

questions.question: Does caching intermediate neural work improve maintenance cost?
questions.consolidated_answer: The tested SC02 cache saved computation but lost runtime in all 20 timing cells.

questions.question: Can required computation span packets smaller than its closure?
questions.consolidated_answer: Yes in CAP01 through carried joint-softmax arithmetic and external layer storage.

questions.question: Is custom hierarchical grouping necessary for that capacity?
questions.consolidated_answer: No in the tested implementation: ordinary multi-pass grouping matched answers and numerical agreement.

questions.question: Does more input reach reliably improve interpretation?
questions.consolidated_answer: Access works; larger-layout mistakes remained. This is not new-rule or deeper transitive reasoning.

questions.question: Can broader preparation improve large-layout behavior without losing the small rule?
questions.consolidated_answer: Yes, bounded in CAP02; 128-task HSA improved with eight-task retention, while 512-task stress remained imperfect.

questions.question: Is the proposed 25,000-language-token maintenance system established?
questions.consolidated_answer: No. No tokenized writer/reader or active-versus-cumulative language-token budget was tested.

questions.question: Are three hierarchy levels optimal, and is the whole NSS lifecycle qualified?
questions.consolidated_answer: Neither. Three is the retained working choice; depth optimization and full lifecycle remain untested.
